metadata.title: ASML Dips Premarket Amid Chip Rout: Dutch Lawmakers Push Back On Proposed US Curbs On Sales To China

content.text:
-
"The MATCH Act is disastrous for ASML, and therefore also for the Dutch economy," Nicole Maes of the conservative VVD party said during a debate on trade policy.
-
Top chip stocks Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) slid 2.5% to 5% in premarket.
-
Retail sentiment was 'bullish' for ASML, 'bearish' for peers AMAT, KLAC and LRCX.
ASML Holding NV (AMSL) shares dipped 3% in early premarket trading on Wednesday amid a broader rout in semiconductor shares, as investors focused on Dutch government deliberations over whether to accept the proposed U.S. curbs on advanced equipment sales to China.
Dutch lawmakers urged the government on Tuesday to push back against proposed legislation that could further restrict the sales of ASML's chip equipment in China, Reuters reported.
The calls came as U.S. Congress mulls whether to attach the bipartisan Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act to the annual defense policy bill, the National Defense Authorization Act.
The bill seeks to curb China's advanced chip production by forcing allies, including the Netherlands and Japan, to adopt tougher export controls or face Washington imposing unilateral restrictions on their equipment, including ASML's immersion deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography tools.
"The MATCH Act is disastrous for ASML, and therefore also for the Dutch economy," Nicole Maes of the conservative VVD party said during a debate on trade policy, according to the Reuters report.
Laurens Dassen of the progressive Volt party urged European measures to shield ASML, saying he believed the U.S. "hates the fact that we have ASML in Europe". Lawmaker Michiel Hoogeveen of the conservative JA21 party called the MATCH Act "unacceptable."
AI Selloff
Like other AI-linked stocks, AMSL faces pressure and has shed about a third of its value from the June peak despite reporting upbeat results quarter after quarter.
On Wednesday, investors were still trying to make sense of the sharp slide in AI bellwether stocks Nvidia (NVDA) and Anthropic (ANT) and whether it signaled a dull outlook for the sector.
Top chip stocks Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) slid 2.5% to 5% in premarket trading, while ASML peers KLA Corp. (KLAC), Lam Research (LRCX) and Applied Materials (AMAT) fell 3.6% to 4.6%.
Retail View For Chip Equipment Stocks
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was 'bullish' for ASML, 'bearish' for peers AMAT, KLAC and LRCX. "$ASML way oversold. Thats very sad," remarked a trader.
